newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Next set for another year of growth.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Next set for another year of growth.

text.p: British fashion and home shopping group Next Plc is expected to turn in another strong performance when it reports annual results next Wednesday.
The retailer has had five years of solid profit and sales growth, and there has been no real sign of any slowdown, retail analysts said.
Pre-tax profits are forecast to rise to between 152 to 157 million stg, up from 125.3 million last year, excluding exceptionals.
The cash-rich company is expected to raise its dividend by about 30 percent to around 15.5 pence a share.
Analysts predicted its retail division should produce double digit sales growth, while its mail order Next Directory could do even better as it has been expanding its customer base.
There are some concerns about the strength of current trading because official statistics have pointed to some softening in consumer demand since January.
"All retailers seem to have had a soft February, but they (Next) will do better than most," said one analyst, who asked not to be identified.
Others were also convinced Next had had a good start to its spring season. "I think current trading will be buoyant," said another analyst.
Next said in January that in the 24 weeks to January 11 total sales grew by 16 percent, with Next Directory up 26 percent and Next Retail up 14 percent.
The market might be looking for news on the group's overseas franchise business, and whether there are plans for more stores in Britain, analysts said.
There will also be interest again in whether there is any chance of some tie-up with Great Universal Stores Plc now Next chairman Lord Wolfson of Sunningdale is now also chairman of GUS.

The shares command a small premium to the retail sector. Roy Maconochie, retail analyst at Henderson Crosthwaite has them on a multiple of 16.6 times based on his forecast for 1997/98. He recommends buying at current levels.
